mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.5% annualized growth rate signals robust economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates and investor risk appetite increases.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0% for three consecutive months signals aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations through higher discount rates and reducing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicate dual economic stress from labor market deterioration and monetary tightening, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced consumer spending and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: The joint effect of rising UNRATE and FEDFUNDS fails to produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a 20-day return regression.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high consumer spending growth (RSAFS > 1.5% monthly), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as retail sector strength drives corporate revenue growth and equity valuations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 1.5% monthly, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals accelerating labor market weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as immediate economic concerns dominate market sentiment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals persistent price pressures that prompt aggressive central bank intervention, reducing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through higher real interest rates and reduced equity attractiveness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% monthly, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profitability, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve implements accommodative monetary policy that boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through lower interest rates and increased liquidity, despite economic weakness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
